items.q: Which national park is famous for its hoodoos?
items.f: On more than 170 nights a year, the temperature at Bryce swings above and below freezing. Water that freezes in cracks helps carve the hoodoos, a process called frost wedging.
items.s: National Park Service: Hoodoos

items.q: In which national park do alligators and crocodiles live side by side?
items.f: South Florida is the only place where America's two native crocodilian species live together.
items.s: National Park Service: American Crocodile

items.q: Which park is often called the 'Galápagos of North America'?
items.f: The islands are home to 145 plant and animal species found nowhere else, including the island fox.
items.s: National Park Service: Island Fox

items.q: How far does Yosemite Falls drop in total?
items.f: It falls in three sections: the 1,430-foot upper fall, 675 feet of middle cascades, and the 320-foot lower fall.
items.s: National Park Service: Yosemite Waterfalls

items.q: Fat Bear Week celebrates the brown bears of which national park?
items.f: Fat Bear Week started in 2014. The bears fatten up on salmon at Brooks Falls before winter.
items.s: National Park Service: Fat Bear Week

items.q: Which national park has the tallest sand dunes in North America?
items.f: Star Dune and Hidden Dune are tied for tallest at about 741 feet. The park is in Colorado.
items.s: National Park Service: Star Dune

items.q: About 95% of which Florida national park is water?
items.f: To see most of the park beyond the visitor center, you need a boat.
items.s: National Park Service: Biscayne National Park

items.q: Which Alaska national park has no roads, trails or campgrounds at all?
items.f: Most visitors fly in on small planes with floats or tundra tires. Experienced hikers count six miles as a good day.
items.s: National Park Service: Gates of the Arctic

items.q: At Saguaro National Park, about how old is a saguaro cactus when it grows its first arm?
items.f: In drier spots, it can take 100 years for a saguaro to grow an arm.
items.s: National Park Service: Saguaro Arms Project

items.q: The General Sherman Tree, the largest tree on Earth by volume, is in which park?
items.f: General Sherman is about 275 feet tall. The latest estimate puts its age at about 2,200 years.
items.s: National Park Service: The General Sherman Tree

items.q: Haleakalā National Park is on which Hawaiian island?
items.f: The summit is 10,023 feet high, and you need a reservation to watch the sunrise from the top.
items.s: National Park Service: Haleakalā Geology

items.q: Which national park gets the most visitors?
items.f: It recorded more than 12 million recreational visits in 2024. There's no entrance fee, but you need a parking tag.
items.s: National Park Service: Great Smoky Mountains Park Statistics

items.q: Which national park is the only one with a stretch of historic Route 66?
items.f: A 1932 Studebaker marks the spot where Route 66 once crossed the park.
items.s: National Park Service: Route 66 Pullout

items.q: For how many miles does the Rio Grande form Big Bend National Park's southern boundary?
items.f: The river's big southward curve through the area gives the park its name.
items.s: National Park Service: The Rio Grande

items.q: Which national park protects the world's longest known cave system?
items.f: Officially, more than 420 miles of passages have been mapped, and explorers are still finding more.
items.s: National Park Service: Additional Miles Added to Mammoth Cave

items.q: In what year was the National Park Service created?
items.f: Woodrow Wilson signed the Organic Act on August 25, 1916, and the NPS celebrates that date as its birthday. Stephen Mather was its first director.
items.s: National Park Service: Creation of the National Park Service

items.q: Which national park has the lowest point in North America?
items.f: Badwater Basin is 282 feet below sea level, and its salt flats cover nearly 200 square miles.
items.s: National Park Service: Badwater Basin

items.q: Which granite wall rises more than 3,000 feet above Yosemite Valley?
items.f: El Capitan is a favorite climb for experienced rock climbers.
items.s: National Park Service: Rock Formations in Yosemite Valley

items.q: Exit Glacier, the only glacier you can drive to in Kenai Fjords, flows from which icefield?
items.f: The Harding Icefield and its glaciers cover about 700 square miles, and at least 38 glaciers flow out of it.
items.s: National Park Service: The Harding Icefield

items.q: Who built Acadia's 45 miles of car-free carriage roads?
items.f: He built them between 1913 and 1940 and paid for 16 of the 17 stone-faced bridges.
items.s: National Park Service: Acadia Carriage Roads

items.q: Which island park in Lake Superior is home to the world's longest-running predator-prey study?
items.f: Scientists have studied the island's wolves and moose since 1958.
items.s: National Park Service: Wolves, an Ecological Study

items.q: How tall is the Grand Teton?
items.f: Elevations in the park range from about 6,320 feet on the valley floor to the Grand Teton's summit.
items.s: National Park Service: Grand Teton Nature

items.q: Which is the only U.S. national park south of the equator?
items.f: The park protects tropical rainforest and Indo-Pacific coral reefs.
items.s: National Park Service: American Samoa Fact Sheet

items.q: White Sands National Park's dunes are made of what?
items.f: The park protects much of the world's largest gypsum dunefield, which covers about 275 square miles.
items.s: National Park Service: White Sands

items.q: What is the most glaciated peak in the contiguous United States?
items.f: Rainier has 28 named glaciers, which cover about 35 square miles.
items.s: National Park Service: Mount Rainier Press Kit

items.q: Which is the smallest U.S. national park?
items.f: The St. Louis park covers about 91 acres.
items.s: National Park Service: Gateway Arch Nature

items.q: How tall is North America's highest peak, in Denali National Park?
items.f: In 2025 the peak's official name went back to Mount McKinley, but the park is still called Denali National Park and Preserve.
items.s: National Park Service: Mountain Name Origins

items.q: From October 7 to March 6, which Acadia summit is the first place in the U.S. to see the sunrise?
items.f: The summit is very popular, so arrive about an hour before sunrise.
items.s: National Park Service: Cadillac Mountain

items.q: What is the highest point on Trail Ridge Road in Rocky Mountain National Park?
items.f: The road runs 48 miles between Estes Park and Grand Lake.
items.s: National Park Service: Trail Ridge Road

items.q: Badlands National Park is famous for what besides its striped buttes?
items.f: It has one of the world's richest fossil mammal beds. Fossils found there include ancient rhinos and saber-toothed cats.
items.s: National Park Service: Paleontology in the White River Badlands

items.q: Which national park has the deepest lake in the United States?
items.f: Crater Lake is 1,943 feet deep. It fills the caldera left when Mount Mazama erupted about 7,700 years ago.
items.s: National Park Service: Crater Lake

items.q: Which park, on Lake Michigan, became the 61st national park in 2019?
items.f: It had been Indiana Dunes National Lakeshore since 1966.
items.s: National Park Service: Indiana Dunes FAQs

items.q: Which West Virginia park became a national park in December 2020?
items.f: It had been a unit of the park system since 1978, when it was designated New River Gorge National River.
items.s: National Park Service: New River Gorge is Now a National Park

items.q: The highest point in Texas is in which national park?
items.f: Guadalupe Peak rises to 8,751 feet. The round-trip hike to the top is 8.4 miles and climbs 3,000 feet.
items.s: National Park Service: Guadalupe Peak

items.q: Before Zion became a national park in 1919, what was it called?
items.f: The canyon became a national monument in 1909, and Congress made it Zion National Park on November 19, 1919.
items.s: National Park Service: Zion People

items.q: Hyperion, the tallest known tree in the world, grows in which park?
items.f: Hyperion is deep off-trail. Hikers trying to reach it have trampled the plants around it, so the park asks people not to go.
items.s: National Park Service: Should I Hike to Hyperion?

items.q: Which scenic road runs the full length of Shenandoah National Park?
items.f: The drive runs 105 miles along the crest of the Blue Ridge Mountains, and it's the park's only public road.
items.s: National Park Service: Driving Skyline Drive

items.q: Which South Carolina national park protects old-growth bottomland hardwood forest and has synchronous fireflies?
items.f: The synchronous fireflies, Photuris frontalis, usually put on their show for about two weeks between mid-May and early June.
items.s: National Park Service: Synchronous Fireflies at Congaree

items.q: Which was the first national park created to protect a cave?
items.f: Theodore Roosevelt signed the bill on January 9, 1903, making Wind Cave the eighth national park.
items.s: National Park Service: A National Park is Created

items.q: Which future president ranched in the North Dakota badlands in the 1880s and now has a national park named for him?
items.f: His Maltese Cross Cabin is on display at the park's South Unit Visitor Center.
items.s: National Park Service: Maltese Cross Cabin

items.q: Which river carved the Grand Canyon?
items.f: The Colorado River runs 277 river miles through the canyon.
items.s: National Park Service: Grand Canyon Geology

items.q: Who is often called the 'Father of the National Parks'?
items.f: Muir's writing helped start a national conservation movement. He also helped create the Sierra Club in 1892.
items.s: National Park Service: National Park Service Remembers John Muir

items.q: Which California park, known for its endangered condors, became a national park in 2013?
items.f: Pinnacles was the 59th national park, and it helps reintroduce California condors to the wild.
items.s: National Park Service: Pinnacles Present Day

items.q: The Hoh Rain Forest is in which national park?
items.f: The Hoh gets an average of about 140 inches of rain a year.
items.s: National Park Service: Visiting the Hoh Rain Forest

items.q: Which national park has more than 2,000 documented natural stone arches?
items.f: The park has the densest concentration of natural stone arches in the world. The longest, Landscape Arch, spans 306 feet.
items.s: National Park Service: Arches

items.q: The Painted Wall, Colorado's tallest cliff, is in which national park?
items.f: The Painted Wall rises 2,250 feet from the river to the rim, and pale bands of pegmatite rock run across it.
items.s: National Park Service: Painted Wall Overlook

items.q: Cuyahoga Valley National Park is in which state?
items.f: The Cuyahoga Valley Scenic Railroad runs 26 miles through the park.
items.s: National Park Service: Scenic Train Ride

items.q: What was Gateway Arch National Park's former name?
items.f: The park covers 90.96 acres along the Mississippi River in St. Louis.
items.s: National Park Service: Gateway Arch History & Culture

items.q: Which two deserts meet in Joshua Tree National Park?
items.f: Joshua trees grow in the higher, cooler Mojave part of the park, while the Colorado Desert lies below 3,000 feet.
items.s: National Park Service: Joshua Tree Map and Brochure

items.q: Cliff Palace, North America's largest cliff dwelling, is in which park?
items.f: Ancestral Puebloan people built Cliff Palace with about 150 rooms.
items.s: National Park Service: Cliff Palace

items.q: Fort Jefferson, a huge 1800s brick fort, is in which national park?
items.f: The park is almost 70 miles west of Key West, and the only way in is by boat or seaplane.
items.s: National Park Service: Dry Tortugas Directions

items.q: At Carlsbad Caverns, visitors gather on summer evenings to watch which animals fly out of the cave?
items.f: Rangers hold a free Bat Flight Program at the cave's Natural Entrance. Cameras and other electronics aren't allowed, to protect the bats.
items.s: National Park Service: Bat Flight Program

items.q: Which park's springs were set aside in 1832, making it the nation's oldest national reservation?
items.f: That was 40 years before Yellowstone became the first national park.
items.s: National Park Service: Yellowstone History FAQs

items.q: Great Basin National Park protects groves of which extremely old trees?
items.f: A bristlecone named Prometheus, cut down in 1964, had 4,862 growth rings.
items.s: National Park Service: The Prometheus Story

items.q: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park includes part of which volcano, the largest active volcano on Earth?
items.f: Mauna Loa rises 13,681 feet above sea level, plus about 30,000 feet more below the sea.
items.s: National Park Service: Mauna Loa

items.q: In 1932, Glacier and Canada's Waterton Lakes together became the world's first what?
items.f: The two parks were later named a joint World Heritage Site in 1995.
items.s: National Park Service: Glacier International Designations

items.q: Which California national park has examples of all four main types of volcanoes?
items.f: Lassen Peak itself is one of the largest plug dome volcanoes in the world.
items.s: National Park Service: Lassen Volcanoes

items.q: Which is the largest U.S. national park?
items.f: At about 13.2 million acres, it's roughly the size of six Yellowstones.
items.s: National Park Service: Wrangell–St. Elias

items.q: At which Utah national park can you pick fruit from historic orchards?
items.f: You can eat ripe fruit in the Fruita orchards for free. Fruit you take with you is paid for at a self-pay station.
items.s: National Park Service: Capitol Reef Orchards
